learning_objective.statement: Apply the store-and-forward idea to a packet moving through intermediate nodes.

experience.title: The Packet's Journey
experience.scenario: A packet needs to travel from Computer A to Computer B. There is no direct physical link between them, so the packet must pass through an intermediate node.
experience.challenge: You are observing the intermediate node as the packet travels through the network. Decide what happens at that node.
experience.learner_action: Choose the sequence that correctly describes how the intermediate node handles the packet.

feedback.correct: Exactly. The intermediate node receives the complete packet, stores it, and then forwards it toward the destination.
feedback.explanation: In the source's description of packet-switched networks, an intermediate node uses store-and-forward: it receives a complete packet, stores it, and then forwards it.

assessment.question: Which sequence best represents store-and-forward at an intermediate node?

options.text: Store → create a new link → forward
Receive part of packet → immediately forward part

mastery_evidence.mastery_signal: correctly applies the store-and-forward sequence to an intermediate node
